tasks.title: Door recall round 2 + bi-fold / cased-opening recall
tasks.notes: Door recall is THE constraint blocking global seal relax. Bi-fold scallop-ink detection shipped; push recall higher via raster-gap detection (symbol-based detectors failed on furniture noise). UNBLOCKED by t15.

prep.what: Improve door chord recall by adding raster-gap detection: identify wall-line endpoints that nearly meet (within door-width range) and treat them as chorded door openings.
prep.understand: t15 (localseal coverage guard) made added chords SAFE — a mistaken chord now auto-reverts via the guard instead of merging two rooms. That safety net means it's OK to be aggressive with chord detection. The bottleneck: chord coverage is near 0% on most sheets (holabird/mitchell/washington/merrimack). Symbol-based ML door detectors failed because furniture noise matches door symbols too closely. The raster-gap approach is simpler: find pairs of nearby wall-line segment endpoints at door-width distances (typically 2.5–4 ft in plan scale), and chord them. The localseal guard handles any false positives automatically.
approach: Review current chord/door detection in `engine/sealfill.py` — understand how bi-fold scallop detection works as a reference model

Implement `detect_raster_gaps(binary_wall_image, scale_pxft)`: scan for near-parallel wall endpoint pairs within door-width range (2–4 ft at plan scale) using distance transforms or endpoint-pair scanning
Add the detected gap midpoints as chord seeds (same interface as existing chord detection) so the localseal guard protects against false positives automatically
Run `python -m gt.harness` on the full corpus and verify: (a) chord coverage metric increases on previously 0%-chord sheets, (b) mean_IoU doesn't drop, (c) gauntlet stays 81/81 green
resources: docs/spike/w13_localseal_guard.py (chord coverage measurements per sheet — your baseline)
